From June 2027, Malaysia's minimum wage jumps from seventeen hundred to two thousand ringgit. So who actually pays for it?
More than four million workers are covered. Those on the minimum get up to three hundred ringgit more a month.
Employers pay first. For a lot of businesses, wages are one of the biggest costs.
And some of that cost can end up in prices. Your nasi lemak, your Grab ride, your groceries.
That's why small businesses with under fifty million ringgit in sales may be exempt, at least for now. The details are still being worked out.
Economists argue both ways. Higher pay means more spending. But too much, too fast, and some hours or jobs could get cut.
